sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. sample of marked blind two-replicate observations \(O_i=(Y_i,X_i,S_{i1},S_{i2})\).
sampling_model.units: Superpopulation units have finite-stratum \(X_i\), compact latent dose \(A_i\), and bounded potential-outcome schedules generated simultaneously as \(Y_i(a)=h(a,X_i,V_i)\) by a jointly measurable response surface, with \(V_i\perp A_i\mid X_i\); the stratum-specific causal means are continuous on \(I\).
sampling_model.treatment: \(S_{i1}=A_i+U_{i1}\) and \(S_{i2}=A_i+U_{i2}\), with independent errors that need not be identically distributed or symmetric and may have spectral gaps; only \(E[U_2]=0\) fixes location.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: At deterministic \(K_n=\lfloor\log n/\log\log n\rfloor\), profile compact order-\(d\) B-spline sieves for \(f_x,q_x\), finite atomic characteristic-function sieves for \(\phi_1,\phi_2\), and \(p_x\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\) against simultaneous empirical probability- and marked-channel restrictions on \(\mathcal D_n\); use the clipped profiled extrema with deterministic tie-breaking and the stated empty-set rule.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Our contributions include establishing identifiability without any assumption on the noise except for coordinate independence.

body.tldr: This is a statistical-inference paper about a causal ADRF under two blind nonidentical asymmetric replicates. Analytic cocycle identification recovers the latent density and marked channel despite remote spectral zeros, and an explicit structural response-surface condition together with causal-mean continuity proves the pointwise causal bridge. The proposed empirical-characteristic-function inversion uses compact signal and error sieves and targets width \(r_n=(\log\log n/\log n)^{\beta-1/2}\), but its constrained-sieve embedding and uniform analytic stability modulus remain unproved. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli lower modulus also remains open, so no matched honest-band rate is yet claimed.

project_justification.gap: Existing statistical results cover blind repeated-measurement density estimation, confidence bands under auxiliary-error, symmetric-error, or fixed-operator designs, and pointwise continuous-treatment inference. They do not give a uniformly honest simultaneous ADRF band under blind nonidentical asymmetric replicate errors with open spectral zero sets, nor the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus needed for a sharp all-band expected-width converse.
project_justification.niche: The inferential niche is a nonlinear severe inverse problem: compact treatment support supplies entire transforms, one centered replicate fixes translation, near-origin conditioning supports local cocycle inversion, and the causal target is a stratum-weighted quotient. A jointly measurable response surface driven by an exogenous random element and continuity of the stratum-specific causal mean bridge that observed regression quotient to the point-dose causal curve.
project_justification.fill: The candidate statistical construction specifies deterministic spline, frequency, truncation, and atomic-sieve dimensions; finite-sample simultaneous radii for the probability, marked, and multinomial coordinates; a compact joint feasibility set; and measurable clipped ADRF extrema. The causal bridge is proved under the explicit structural and continuity conditions. The remaining upper-side task is a shape-preserving feasible embedding and a quantitative discrete analytic-cocycle modulus; the lower-side task is the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus. Until both are proved, the advertised \(r_n\) rate is a target rather than an established matched rate.

body.related_work: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy provide the unmarked probability-channel cocycle, constrained polynomial estimator, and compact-support \(L^2\) minimax experiment that inform the analytic machinery; their qualitative identification theorem requires neither the fixed \(q_e\)-moment radius nor the uniform pair \((\nu_0,c_0)\), which are paper-specific quantitative restrictions here. Gassiat, Le Corff, and Lehéricy supply the broader analytic-continuation principle for blind deconvolution. Huang and Zhang formulate the error-contaminated continuous-treatment ADRF and derive pointwise inference with a known everywhere-nonzero error transform. Kato and Sasaki (2018) develop deconvolution bands with an unknown error distribution using an auxiliary error sample, together with a symmetric-error repeated-measurement route; that design differs from two blind nonidentical asymmetric replicates and has neither the marked quotient nor joint cell-mass profiling. Kato and Sasaki (2019) obtain multiplier-bootstrap uniform bands for errors-in-variables regression under conventional spectral conditions. Kato, Sasaki, and Ura invert Kotlarski moment restrictions to retain coverage without completeness, but do not give a sharp shrinking-width result for a marked quotient. Babii gives honest expected-diameter control for fixed linear inverse operators. Low supplies the testing-to-expected-length reduction used only after the marked modulus is established. These papers inform separate components of the statistical argument; none is presented as a theorem literally tightened by the enabling identification result.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The pointwise causal bridge is closed by the structural response-surface and continuity conditions, and the qualitative marked identification is already established. The upper claim still stands or falls on a uniform discrete analytic-cocycle stability inequality and a shape-preserving constrained-sieve embedding. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus remains the separate lower-bound kernel.
body.honest_scope: The fixed values of \(\beta\), the Sobolev radii, \(p_{\min}\), the moment and local spectral constants, and \(\kappa\) are known class indices. Causal interpretation additionally uses a jointly measurable structural response surface with an exogenous latent variable and continuity of each stratum-specific causal mean on \(I\); these conditions are compatible with the common-uniform Bernoulli lower construction and do not strengthen measurement-error assumptions. Adaptation, growing replicate counts, boundary bands, and computational optimization remain outside scope. The explicit simultaneous upper band and matching all-band converse are not yet established because the analytic stability and fixed-nuisance lower-modulus steps remain open.
body.interpretation: The observed two-channel law identifies the continuous regression curve \(q_x/f_x\). Structural exogeneity first equates this curve with the stratum-specific causal mean almost everywhere in dose; positivity and continuity then extend the equality to every target dose. Coordinatewise weak unconfoundedness and almost-sure consistency alone would not suffice because they permit treatment-dependent diagonal modifications on null sets.
